title: THE SYMBOL THAT HEALS… OR DECEIVES?
paragraphs:
THE SYMBOL THAT HEALS… OR DECEIVES?
What the Pharmaceutical Logo Really Means—and Why the Cross Still Stands Above It All
You’ve seen it your whole life.
On hospitals. On medicine bottles. On ambulances rushing through the night while someone fights for their life in the back.
A serpent… wrapped around a staff.
And maybe—just maybe—you’ve wondered in silence…
Because if you’ve ever opened the Scriptures… if you’ve ever lingered long enough in the ancient text… you know the serpent is not neutral.
It slithers into Eden before it ever appears on a medical emblem.

“וְהַנָּחָשׁ הָיָה עָרוּם”
Veha-nachash hayah arum
“Now the serpent was more crafty…” (Genesis 3:1)
That same creature whispered doubt into humanity’s first breath of innocence.
So why is it now a global symbol of healing?
Let’s go deeper than surface-level fear. Let’s go where truth actually lives.
Because not everything that looks suspicious is sinister—and not everything that looks harmless is holy.
There is a moment in Scripture most people skip past too quickly.
It doesn’t fit neatly into Sunday school illustrations.
But it holds the key to this question.
Israel is wandering in the wilderness—tired, complaining, spiritually drifting. And suddenly… judgment comes in the form of serpents.
Fiery serpents. Venom. Death spreading through the camp.
Realising too late that rebellion has consequences.
Then God does something that, at first glance, feels shocking.

“עֲשֵׂה לְךָ שָׂרָף… וְשִׂים אֹתוֹ עַל־נֵס”
Aseh lecha saraph… vesim oto al-nes
“Make a fiery serpent… and set it on a pole.” (Numbers 21:8)
God… tells Moses… to make a serpent?
The very image of the curse… becomes the instrument of healing.

“וְהָיָה כָּל־הַנָּשׁוּךְ… וְרָאָה אֹתוֹ וָחָי”
“Everyone who is bitten… when he looks at it, shall live.”
Healing didn’t come by ignoring the problem.
Trusting God in the middle of it.
Jesus Himself brings this moment back into focus.
“And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up…” (John 3:14)

“Καὶ καθὼς Μωϋσῆς ὕψωσεν τὸν ὄφιν…”
Kai kathōs Mōusēs hypsōsen ton ophin…
Jesus connects Himself… to that serpent on the pole.
But because He took on what was killing us.
The serpent on the staff was never about glorifying evil.
It was about exposing it… and defeating it through obedience and faith.
So what about the pharmaceutical symbol?
Historically, the Rod of Asclepius comes from ancient Greek medicine—yes, rooted in a pagan context.
But here’s where discernment becomes deeper than fear.
But they can also be reinterpreted through truth.
The question isn’t “Is there pagan origin?”
Because no logo can save you.
No system can redeem your soul.

“בּוֹ נִרְפָּאנוּ”
Bo nirpa’nu
“By Him we are healed.” (Isaiah 53:5)
And yet… God still uses imperfect systems.
Even symbols that once meant something else.
Because grace has a way of rewriting stories that were never supposed to end in redemption.
But let’s be honest for a moment.
Some of you reading this aren’t wrestling with symbols.
Maybe even betrayed by systems that were supposed to help you.
You’re searching for something pure… something true… something you can actually hold onto.
He heals what no human hand can reach.
And still… He works through people.
Because He is not limited by what He uses.
He is defined by who He is.
The pharmaceutical symbol is not secretly controlling your soul.
But your soul can be lost if you place your ultimate trust anywhere but Christ.
Or maybe… come to Him for the first time.
Because everything—every symbol, every system, every story—must bow to the Cross.
There are people reading your comment who will stand with you… who needed to see that they’re not alone.
You’re going to need to revisit this when confusion tries to come back.
And if you want to go deeper—if you want real discipleship, real truth, real growth in Christ…
And yes… supporting what spreads the Gospel matters.
If your heart is hungry… don’t ignore that.
This was the moment God used to wake something up inside you again.
The serpent was lifted… but only the Savior was crucified for you.
